title: Self-hosted business email at a fraction of the cost
context: Client with several brands and a growing team, previously on Hostinger business email

stats.label: delivery, not spam, via a reputable sending IP

problem: The client had signed up for Hostinger email on a heavily discounted first term. When the plan came up for renewal the price jumped several times over, and by then they needed more mailboxes and more storage than the plan allowed. Paying per mailbox for every brand and every new hire was going to scale badly.
approach: Researched self-hosted options and chose mailcow, a Dockerised mail stack with Postfix, Dovecot, Rspamd spam filtering, SOGo webmail, and a web admin panel, running on a single VPS.
Set up DNS authentication for every domain: SPF records, DKIM signing keys generated by mailcow, and a DMARC policy, so receiving servers can verify the mail is legitimate.
Routed outbound mail through Postmark's SMTP relay so messages leave from an IP with an established reputation instead of a fresh VPS address that inbox providers distrust.
Migrated existing mailboxes and configured the team's clients, with webmail available as a fallback from any browser.
Automated backups of mail data and configuration, with TLS certificates renewed automatically.
result: Recurring cost dropped by roughly 95%, from per-mailbox subscriptions to a single VPS bill plus a small relay fee. The client can now add mailboxes, domains, and storage without changing plans, and mail lands in the inbox rather than the spam folder.

title: WhatsApp receipts and account updates straight from the POS, with no per-message fee
context: Retail client running the web-based POS, invoices previously sent by hand

stats.label: receipt or invoice sent at checkout
payment, balance and store-credit updates for account customers
staff link the business WhatsApp from inside the POS

problem: Cashiers were sending invoices and receipts by hand: download the PDF from the POS, open WhatsApp, find the customer, attach, send. At rush hour that queue of small tasks slowed the counter and receipts went out late or not at all. A marketing company offered a WhatsApp and SMS integration, but it was priced per message through a third-party API, which for a high-volume retail counter would have added a large recurring bill for something as basic as a receipt.
approach: Built a WhatsApp messaging module that drives WhatsApp Web through a headless Chromium instance hosted on the client's own server, so there is no per-message API charge.
Connected it to the POS so a receipt or invoice goes to the customer's number automatically at checkout, PDF attached, and the delivery module notifies customers when an order is on its way.

Added account messages for credit customers: the moment a payment on their ledger is processed they receive a message confirming the amount paid, their outstanding balance, and any store credit available, so account holders never have to call in to ask where they stand.
Added a login and logout flow inside the POS: staff scan a QR code to link the business WhatsApp account and can unlink it the same way, without touching the server.
Hardened the session handling: authentication keys are hashed and the session state is stored in the database, so the link survives restarts and redeploys and cannot be lifted from the filesystem.
Made the service resilient to disconnects with automatic reconnection and clear status in the POS when the link needs re-scanning.
result: Receipts and invoices now leave the POS the moment a sale closes, with no download step and no one tied up at the counter, and credit customers get a balance update the instant a payment is booked. The client got the integration the marketing company was selling, minus the per-message pricing, running on infrastructure they already pay for.
